title: Bipolar Displacement of the Lung Macrophage Ecosystem in Interstitial Lung Disease
content: Background: In interstitial lung disease (ILD), alveolar macrophage loss and SPP1+ expansion have been described separately; the lost side (the homeostatic reservoir) is rarely quantified on a common scale or at donor level. We tested whether ILD remodels the lung macrophage ecosystem as a bipolar displacement of relative composition.Methods: A 25-module functional/morphological scoring system was applied to three scRNA-seq atlases (Madissoon normal lung, 40,634 myeloid cells; a PBMC reference; the Natri ILD atlas, 175,426 cells, 118 donors, 10 diagnoses, 30 microclusters), normal-lung Visium sections, 195,994 ligand-receptor edges and the independent IPF Cell Atlas (GSE136831), with donor-level statistics as the primary inferential unit.Results: Interstitial macrophages (IMs) were the most reprogrammed compartment, losing complement/phagocytic identity (up to -0.39) while gaining granuloma and matrix-remodelling programmes; sarcoidosis was the exception (complement +0.08; antigen presentation +0.31). C1Q-high reservoir microclusters, CD10/MME-high in their lipid-handling branch, contracted at donor level across all powered diagnoses, with disease-specific expansion of SPP1+ states; in IPF, donor-level tests supported a candidate SPP1/CHIT1-high state (mc26, 5.3% versus 0.39%; p=1.6×10-9; microcluster boundaries seed-sensitive) and a candidate OCSTAMP+ fusion-primed IM state. Ligand-receptor analysis indicated strengthened FN1-ITGB1/SPP1-CD44 axes and attenuated THBS1-CD36/C3 circuits; spatial data showed dispersed, non-aggregated homeostatic behaviour in normal lung; the expanding pole and the compositional anticorrelation replicated in the independent cohort, whereas programme-level identity loss did not.Conclusions: The ILD macrophage ecosystem exhibits a bipolar displacement of relative composition: a testable model of homeostatic-niche dissolution and pathological-niche construction.
